sections.title: Construction Insurance Types and Accounting
sections.content:
Construction insurance represents a significant cost center, typically 5-12% of revenue, and requires careful accounting treatment for proper job costing and financial reporting.

## Workers' Compensation Insurance

Workers' compensation is the largest insurance cost for most contractors:

**Rating Structure:**
- Experience modification rate (EMR or X-mod)
- Classification codes by trade
- Payroll basis (cost per $100 of payroll)

**Example Rates by Trade:**
- Carpentry: $15-25 per $100 payroll
- Concrete work: $20-30 per $100
- Roofing: $40-60 per $100 (high risk)
- Electrical: $8-12 per $100 (lower risk)

**Accounting Treatment:**

Deposit method (pay-as-you-go):
```
Monthly based on actual payroll:
DR Workers' Comp Insurance Expense       $XXX
   CR Cash                                      $XXX

Allocate to jobs based on labor:
DR CIP - Job A - Insurance                $XXX
DR CIP - Job B - Insurance                $XXX
   CR Workers' Comp Allocation                  $XXX
```

Audit adjustment at year-end reconciles deposit to actual exposure.
